trigger_phrase_or_event: copy locked in package before prompt/image handoff

copy_lock.copy:
You disappointed me.
For a while,
that was all I saw.

Hurt can make
one moment look like
a whole person.

I began judging
every memory
through that moment.

But pain knows
what happened,
not everything about you.
So I looked at you again.

You had disappointed me.
You were not
a disappointment.

visual_system_candidates.name: Cinematic Obstruction-to-Clearing Sequence

slide_visual_blueprint.copy:

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Late-night dining room, medium-wide diagonal geography shot from Aachu's side of the table. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu sits in the lower-left at a table set for two, still and upright rather than collapsed or crying. One visibly cold, untouched second plate, a serving bowl with a settled surface, and a burned-low plain candle prove she waited. The single empty chair intended for Zuv dominates the center foreground and creates a physical barrier. Zuv has just entered through the background doorway, rain-damp and stopped mid-step when he sees the table; he is present but visually smaller than the empty chair. His phone and keys remain in his own hands for this arrival beat. Aachu looks at the empty chair, not at him. The visual must read without copy as: he promised to be here, he was not, and his absence has become the first thing she sees. Exactly two people; no restaurant, server, flowers, gifts, background people, portraits, readable clock numbers, random lettering, or melodramatic tears.
slide_visual_blueprint.must_show: Visible Aachu/Zuv relationship behavior that proves the exact copy.

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Same late-night dining room seconds later, low table-level view from just behind Aachu's right shoulder. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. The empty chair back fills the middle plane and clearly occludes part of Zuv's torso without intersecting or merging with him, so Aachu sees him through the geometry of the chair that represented his absence. Zuv is now fully inside the room. His keys already rest on a small side ledge; with one anatomically attached right hand, he deliberately places his phone face-down beside them, away from the table, while his left hand hangs open and empty at his side. He then stays beyond the chair rather than approaching or explaining with gestures. Aachu's partial profile and shoulder remain in the near foreground, her eye-line fixed through the chair slats toward him. The cold plate and burned-low candle stay visible at opposite lower corners. Camera compression makes the chair feel larger than him while keeping clear depth separation. No reflection, extra person, bouquet, apology note, speech bubble, readable clock, or random text.

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Later that night, a wide single-person hallway shot with exactly Aachu and no live background figure. A short row of three small framed memories sits on a narrow console. Their interiors use only soft, non-figurative washes of the couple's recurring clothing colors, with no discernible faces or bodies. Two frames are already face-down, showing only plain backs. The dining room and Zuv are absent from view, but the cooled blue night light matches slides 1-2. slide_visual_blueprint.copy: So I looked at you again.
slide_visual_blueprint.scene: EDIT-TARGET COMPOSITION LOCK: rebuild the supplied failed proof as a table-across medium two-shot, not a side-by-side portrait. In the same sparse morning dining room, Aachu sits on the left side of a small rectangular table and Zuv sits on the opposite right side; a clearly visible strip of tabletop and open conversational distance separate their torsos. Frame both people from head through lap, with exactly Aachu and Zuv and all four hands fully visible. Low at the center foreground on the tabletop, place one genuinely palm-sized memory frame with no easel or kickstand. Freeze the physical action midway: the frame's bottom edge remains visibly planted on the tabletop, the frame plane is tilted only about forty-five degrees above the table, its plain blank back faces the viewer, and Aachu's attached right fingertips support one side edge. Her left hand stays open on her own thigh. Zuv sits upright opposite, both open hands separate on his own thighs, without reaching or leaning. Aachu has just moved her eyes from the frame to Zuv; they meet a direct unobstructed eye-line with neutral closed mouths, serious-soft faces, and no smile. Preserve guarded space: no touch, romantic inward lean, cuddling, or already-reconciled pose. At the far lower-left corner show only a thin cropped rim of one cold plate—no fork, food residue, full plate, cup, or meal spread. The background is only neutral warm-ivory paper grain plus a faint non-figurative window-light wash: no plant or foliage, shelf, cabinet, books, wall art, photograph, other frame, mirror, reflection, logo, sign, or decorative object. Exactly two human depictions total. Render no lettering anywhere on skin, clothing, furniture, props, or background. The only visible text in the entire image is the exact slide line 'So I looked at you again.' and the tiny top-right brandmark '@a.storyof.two'.
slide_visual_blueprint.must_show: A palm-sized frame visibly halfway through its lift, all four story-required hands, direct gaze, exact wardrobe, and no figurative background object.

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Matched wide release using the same dining-room camera axis as slide 1, now in clear morning light. Exactly Aachu and Zuv and exactly two dining chairs. Aachu remains seated in her original chair. Zuv remains seated in the same once-empty chair from slides 1 and 4, but he has pulled and rotated that chair around to the adjacent side of the table, moving its back out of their sightline and leaving no third chair. Their body distance is conversational and smaller than slide 4, without a celebratory embrace. The cold plate and burned-out candle remain at the far edge of the table, proving the hurt was not erased. One memory frame stands upright near Aachu with its plain back toward the viewer; the other two stay face-down on the distant hallway console, making the ending a beginning rather than a magical restoration. Aachu speaks or listens with one relaxed hand open on the tabletop; Zuv listens with both hands visible and separate, no touching yet. Their faces are calm and fully recognizable. The image must read without copy as: the event is still part of the room, but it is no longer the only thing between them. No third chair, cleaned table, fresh meal, flowers, gifts, hug, kiss, halo light, hearts, background figure, live reflection, or instant-happy ending.
